page.title: tinyactors compared with Durable Objects
page.description: Where a stateful session runs, what an idle one keeps, how its tests move time, what a deploy does to it, and when Cloudflare Durable Objects are the better choice.

hero.headline: Stateful sessions in the backend you already run
hero.lede: A Durable Object gives each agent session its own state and one order of events, on Cloudflare's network. tinyactors runs that session as a statechart inside your own process. Choose Durable Objects when sessions must be reachable from anywhere in the world.

section.heading: Cloudflare runs the object; you run the host
section.p: Your backend already runs somewhere you chose. A session's logic in a Durable Object runs on Cloudflare's network instead, wherever the rest of your backend lives.

claim.statement: A Durable Object is a Worker with storage
claim.p: Cloudflare defines it as a special kind of Worker that combines compute with storage. It is placed close to where it is first requested.
Each object has a globally unique name, so a request reaches that one object from anywhere in the world.

claim.statement: A tinyactors host lives in your program
claim.p: new Host(charts, options) runs the actors inside the Node.js, Bun, Python or browser process that imports the package.
A chart reaches the model's API, your database or a socket only through handlers you give the host.
claim.source: Home, "The chart decides, your code acts"
I/O processors, "Ask for outside work with a send"

section.p: The cost is on your side. Your program decides where each host runs and carries a message to another host's actor (). On Cloudflare, that's the platform's work.

section.heading: Idle sessions wait in your database
section.p: Most sessions sit idle between a user's messages. Their state must survive until the next one, without holding memory meanwhile.

claim.statement: An idle object discards its memory
claim.p: After 10 seconds without work an object can hibernate, and its in-memory state is discarded. Cloudflare says to persist anything important to the object's storage.
That storage is SQLite, up to 10 GB per object on the paid plan.
claim.source: Cloudflare, "In-memory state in a Durable Object"

claim.statement: An idle actor goes to your store whole
claim.p: Give the host a store and a bound, and it writes the actors past the bound into the store: variables, active states and all. The next event wakes one.
Two million actors ran with at most 1000 in memory and the rest in SQLite.
claim.source: Hibernation, "Cap how many actors stay in memory"
Hibernation, "Run two million actors with 1000 in memory"

section.p: An actor in memory takes about 530 bytes of a Node.js process holding a million, measured with a counter chart of one variable ().

section.heading: Test a thousand timeouts in one program
section.p: A session's bugs hide in what happens when an answer is late. This payment charges a card, charges again after 30 seconds without an answer and gives up after three charges:
The test's stand-in provider answers at once, 45 seconds late or never. A simulated clock jumps to each timeout, so a thousand payments run in one Node.js process:

claim.statement: Durable Objects' tests run in the Workers runtime
claim.p: Cloudflare's Vitest integration runs tests inside the Workers runtime, with the objects' bindings and storage.
runDurableObjectAlarm() fires a scheduled alarm at once instead of waiting for its timer.

claim.statement: A simulated clock moves when tests move it
claim.p: The test above is a host, a clock and a stand-in object. Every timer of every actor waits for clock.increment().
claim.source: Testing, "Replace the chart's services and its clock"

section.heading: Ship new rules to running sessions
section.p: You deploy a turn limit while thousands of sessions are mid-conversation. Each one must keep the turns it already counted.

claim.statement: A deploy resets an active object
claim.p: By default an active object keeps its old code until it hibernates, or for up to 300 seconds. Then it resets and adopts the new code.
Hibernation discards in-memory state, so what carries over is what the object stored.

claim.statement: A migration moves running actors to a version
claim.p: host.addImage() adds the new chart to the running host, and host.migrate() moves actors to it.
Each keeps its active states, queue and delayed sends. The new chart reads the old variables from one event.
claim.source: Migration, "Move the actors and carry their variables"

section.p: Ten thousand agent sessions answer three prompts each, with at most 100 in memory. Version 2 adds a limit of three turns, and one migration moves every session, hibernated ones included:
Every session kept its count through the move. So each one ended at the limit instead of asking the model again.

section.heading: A crash keeps what was written down
section.p: A machine dies halfway through a session. Both answers start from storage; they differ in who owns it.

claim.statement: An object's writes are stored all or none
claim.p: If a machine fails, either all of a write's changes reached disk or none did.
Point-in-time recovery restores an object's database to any moment of the past 30 days.

claim.statement: A crash keeps what your program saved
claim.p: Actors live in your process's memory, so a crash stops them all. Hibernated actors in your store and the last snapshot come back.
Inputs after that snapshot return when your program journaled them.
claim.source: When to use tinyactors, "A crash stops memory and keeps saved state"

section.heading: Choose tinyactors for sessions inside your backend

item.term: A backend on the cloud you chose
item.text: The host is a library in your Node.js, Bun or Python process, so the sessions deploy with the code that calls them.

item.term: Deploys that keep each session's place
item.text: A migration moves running sessions to new rules with their states, queues and timers.
A simulated clock jumps to each deadline, so one program checks a thousand sessions.

item.term: Logic an agent can write and you can read
item.text: Each session is one SCXML chart, and an uploaded chart runs in the QuickJS sandbox.

section.heading: Choose Durable Objects for sessions reached from anywhere

item.text: Each object has a globally unique name and is placed near its first request. tinyactors leaves placement and failover between hosts to your program.
Each object has its own SQLite database, restorable to any point of the past 30 days.
WebSocket Hibernation keeps clients connected while the object is out of memory, and duration charges stop meanwhile.
A Durable Object is a Worker, so it shares the platform, bindings and deploys of the rest of the application.
